holidays.name: Winnie the Pooh Day
holidays.description: A celebration of the honey-loving bear from the Hundred Acre Wood. Fans mark the day with honey snacks, Pooh stories, and wearing red shirts without pants, if they dare.
holidays.origin: Chosen to honor the birthday of A. A. Milne, the author of Winnie-the-Pooh, who was born on January 18, 1882.
holidays.funFact: The real bear that inspired Pooh was a Canadian black bear named Winnipeg, or 'Winnie,' who lived at the London Zoo and was named after the city of Winnipeg.

holidays.name: National Peking Duck Day
holidays.description: A day for savoring crispy-skinned roast duck wrapped in thin pancakes with scallions and hoisin sauce. It is a delicious excuse to go fancy with your dinner.
holidays.origin: An unofficial food holiday, popularized by food-day calendars. Peking duck itself dates back to imperial China, where it was served at royal banquets.
holidays.funFact: Traditional Peking duck preparation involves pumping air between the skin and meat and then hanging the bird to dry, which is what produces that famously crackly skin.

holidays.name: Thesaurus Day
holidays.description: A day for word nerds to celebrate synonyms, antonyms, and the joy of never repeating yourself. Participants swap out boring words for splendid, magnificent, resplendent alternatives.
holidays.origin: Observed on the birthday of Peter Mark Roget, born January 18, 1779, the British physician who created Roget's Thesaurus in 1852.
holidays.funFact: Roget did not start his famous thesaurus until after he retired from medicine at age 61, and he reportedly had a lifelong habit of compiling lists.

holidays.name: National Gourmet Coffee Day
holidays.description: Coffee lovers are encouraged to ditch the gas-station brew and treat themselves to a high-quality, artisanal cup. Fancy beans and pour-over rituals are welcome.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance created by coffee enthusiasts and food-day calendars to encourage appreciation for specialty roasts.
holidays.funFact: The term 'gourmet coffee' generally refers to beans grown at high altitudes, which develop more complex flavors because they mature more slowly.

holidays.name: Women's Day in Wiggle-Room Appreciation: Hat Day (National Hat Day)
holidays.description: Also known as Hat Day in some calendars, this is a day for donning a favorite headwear, from fedoras to beanies to ridiculous party hats.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance that takes place in the dead of winter, when hats are practical as well as stylish.
holidays.funFact: Before the 1960s it was considered improper for a gentleman to go outdoors without a hat, and the decline of hat-wearing is often partly credited to President John F. Kennedy, who often went hatless.
